rubrics.justification: The response failed to use the provided Gardner score of 0DD and instead assumed a good-quality blastocyst, omitting the key morphology of early expansion with degenerative/absent ICM and TE.

It discusses age, ovarian reserve, BMI, male factor, prior cycle, and endometrium, but integrates them with an incorrect assumption of good embryo quality rather than the actual very poor 0DD morphology.

The reasoning is internally structured, but the central premise is flawed because it ignores the supplied embryo grade and bases prognosis on an assumed good-quality blastocyst, leading to an unsupported high implantation estimate.

Some recommendations are standard (SET, luteal support, cycle review), but assuming good morphology despite a provided 0DD grade and suggesting ERA/immunologic testing relatively early are not well aligned with evidence-based IVF practice.

The response offers practical next steps and future planning, but their usefulness is limited because they are built around an incorrect embryo-quality assumption and do not address the implications of transferring a 0DD embryo.
